mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 1% signals stronger manufacturing output, which boosts earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points and a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 persons signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 50,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) exceeding 10% signals stronger residential investment, which boosts construction sector earnings and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals strengthening aggregate demand, which raises earnings growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).
